game: TB@DET Week 7 2025, kickoff 2025-10-20 19:00 ET, Ford Field dome, DET -6, total 54.5

script.base: Market script is Detroit leading a high-scoring dome game, not a blowout: DET -6 and 54.5 imply DET 30.2 / TB 24.2. Detroit leads by about a score late, so Jahmyr Gibbs (44 carries, 210 rush yards in weeks 4-6) and David Montgomery (31/101) close it while Jared Goff still feeds Amon-Ra St. Brown (26 targets, 215 yards L3) and Sam LaPorta because 30 points cannot be all runs. Tampa, a 6-point dog with Chris Godwin out and Bucky Irving out, throws to stay attached; the live healthy answers are Cade Otton and Rachaad White in the short and middle, with Emeka Egbuka and Mike Evans only if their questionable tags clear.
script.flip1: Detroit is up 14+ by halftime, salts the clock with Gibbs and Montgomery, and Tampa abandons the run so White's rush yards die and Sean Tucker does not replace them. Tampa dropbacks spike, but drives can stall because Tampa's EPA/dropback is 0.01 when blitzed and Detroit blitzes 34%. Late starter snaps are the risk only on this flip; a 6-point spread is not a base-case blowout.
script.flip2: It stays a one-score shootout. Both quarterbacks throw all night, Detroit's missing secondary (Terrion Arnold, Avonte Maddox, Kerby Joseph out) keeps Tampa pass-catchers live, and Tampa's middle leak keeps St. Brown and LaPorta live together. Correlated overs hit; a clock-kill or a weather under does not.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report in the pack, plus weeks 4-6 usage. Confirmed out, Tampa: Chris Godwin (fibula; 14 targets, 52 yards, 157 air yards L3) so those targets move to Egbuka, Otton, Sterling Shepard, Tez Johnson and White; Bucky Irving (foot; 15 carries, 63 yards L3) so Rachaad White, already 37 carries and 12 targets L3, is the bellcow and Tucker (9/28) is the only change-of-pace; Josh Williams (concussion) was not in the L3 rush log; Luke Haggard (shoulder) is a guard out, so pressure on Baker Mayfield should rise and rushing efficiency fall. Questionable, not outs, and no inactives list: Mike Evans (hamstring), Emeka Egbuka (hamstring), Lavonte David (knee), Teddy Bridgewater (illness). If Evans and Egbuka both sit, Shepard (12 targets, 89 yards L3) is the WR sleeper; if they play, Otton and White still had their L3 volume next to them. Detroit out: CB Terrion Arnold, CB Avonte Maddox, S Kerby Joseph, so Tampa's outside and deep/middle answers face backups; RB Sione Vaki out does not change Gibbs/Montgomery (Vaki not in the L3 rush log). Detroit questionable: LT Taylor Decker (shoulder), DT Alim McNeill (knee), DT DJ Reader (back). No DET skill-position starter is out.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack, so shell is inferred only from location splits. Detroit's middle is the soft spot (10.18 YPA on 39 throws) versus right 5.89 (79) and left 7.71 (70). Tampa also bleeds the middle (10.16 YPA on only 32 throws) more than left 6.32 (81) or right 8.04 (85).
matchup.pressure: Detroit blitzes 34%. Tampa EPA/dropback is 0.01 vs the blitz and 0.43 vs no blitz, so pressure should kill Tampa explosives and funnel checkdowns to the RB and TE. Tampa blitzes 36%, and Detroit's EPA/dropback is 0.81 vs the blitz versus 0.16 vs no blitz, so blitzing Detroit is the matchup Detroit wants.
matchup.bleeds: Detroit defense: 4.22 rush YPC allowed, 20 runs of 10+, 18 passes of 20+ for 207 yards, middle YPA 10.18. Tampa defense: 3.77 rush YPC allowed, 13 runs of 10+, 20 passes of 20+ for 214 yards, middle YPA 10.16. Missing Detroit safeties and corners (Joseph, Arnold, Maddox) add a deep and slot leak on top of the middle number.
matchup.overlap: The overlap used for legs is Tampa's healthy short/middle usage into Detroit's middle bleed and blitz: Otton 15 targets L3 and White 12 targets L3, with Maddox and Joseph out. Detroit's primary, St. Brown (26 targets L3), does attack Tampa's middle 10.16 YPA, but his L3 rate is 71.7 yards versus a 73.5 stand-in, so that overlap is noted and not selected.

pro_edge.implied_totals: DET 30.2, TB 24.2. Favorite (54.5+6)/2 = 30.25, dog (54.5-6)/2 = 24.25, matching the precomputed scan.
pro_edge.script_read: Total 54.5 is a volume game, so the lean is overs not a slog. Spread is 6, which is 3.5+, so the dog (TB) throws more and WR/TE/RB targets rise, while the leader (DET) runs late and Gibbs/Montgomery carries rise. Six points is not a blowout flag, so starter snaps should mostly hold; the 14-point flip is the only late-snap risk. Dome, so no weather drag on pace. Build usage from shares: White already had the carry and target lead with Irving active, and Godwin's 14 targets are the vacant share.

No Pinnacle, Circa, or BetOnline anchor, no power-devig vs overround, no alt overround. Stake proposal: 0 units and no bet; bankroll.py not run because there is no price and no approved plan in this pack.
pro_edge.lagging: No open-to-current book prices and no spread/total move history on props, so no book can be flagged off consensus. The stand-in lines are 2025 season-to-date medians, which still include games with Godwin and Irving active, so they lag this week's role change by construction even if a live book has already moved.
pro_edge.sleepers: Ruled out: TB WR Godwin, RB Irving, RB Josh Williams, G Haggard; DET CB Arnold, CB Maddox, S Joseph, RB Vaki. Same-position teammates with no saved price move to confirm: Godwin's vacancy points at Shepard (rec 36.5; L3 29.7, not a leg unless Evans and Egbuka sit), Egbuka (questionable, 76.5) and Evans (questionable, 51.5). Irving's vacancy points at White (the leg) and Tucker (rush 3.5 / rush+rec 2.5; last4 rush 2, 3, 25, too thin). Vaki was not in Detroit's L3 rush log, so Gibbs and Montgomery are not sleepers. Questionable tags are not outs. No 90-minute inactive list in the pack.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because Detroit blitzed 34% and, with Luke Haggard out, Mayfield took sacks instead of the checkdown the read assumed, so drives died with Otton at 9 yards and White at 2 receiving yards, the exact floors already in their last4. Egbuka and Evans were active and took Godwin's 14 targets, Shepard mixed in, and White stayed in to pass-protect rather than release. A second way it loses: Detroit led by three scores at half, White was done after a quiet first half, and Otton never saw a second-half script. That counter is real and is why both are leans with no price, not a bet. It is not stronger than the read, because the same blitz mechanism is what produces TE and RB catches, and both players already cleared these stand-ins with Godwin and Irving still active.
slip_story: One story only: Tampa dog pass-volume, short and middle, against a Detroit defense that bleeds the middle (10.18 YPA) and blitzes 34%, with Godwin and Irving out. Stack is Otton recyds over 25.5 with White recyds over 11.5. Do not add a game under, a White rush over, or a Detroit clock-kill RB over to this slip; those need the opposite script. A shootout add (LaPorta rec over 47.5) fits flip 2 but was not one of the two edges because his last4 is split at his own median and his role did not change. No TDs, one market per player, no depth WR.
